title: Paradigmes des courbes algébriques (version provisoire) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the previous pages try to describe a groupoid Λ over a group π, with a set of 'boundary' objects T = ∂Λ, in a way that is compatible with an outer action of a group (Σ, later Γ) on π. Grothendieck finds that approach unilluminating ('Ce n'est pas bien éclairant') and tries a more functorial one here.

Setting. Π is a connected 'space' (presumably a topos or space whose fundamental group is π), with universal covering Π̃. Its category of coverings Rev(Π) is equivalent to π-Ens (π-sets) via E ↦ Π̃ ×_π E. This is the vertical ≀↑ arrow, with a struck-out decoration F̃₀ next to it.

Step 1: functors given by a right π-set. One takes a functor F : Rev(Π) → (Ens). Transported to π-Ens, it is E ↦ τ° ∧_π E, a contracted product with a right π-set τ. The NB says the index ° marks that the π-operations have been dropped from the result, so that only the underlying set remains. It also says these are exactly the functors commuting with arbitrary inductive limits (lim→ quelconques). This is the standard fact that colimit-preserving functors π-Ens → Ens correspond to right π-sets, the 'tensoring with a module' description of cocontinuous functors on a presheaf topos B_π. In the intended application τ is a 'disjoint' union of principal π-sets, attached to the boundary T. This links to the previous page, where the stabilizers π_t give a family of subgroups indexed by T/π.

Step 2: compatibility with the outer action. Now let γ range over a group Γ acting on Π, hence acting on π only by outer automorphisms. One requires isomorphisms F(^γΠ') ≃ F(Π'), functorial in the covering Π' ∈ Rev Π and transitive (a cocycle condition) in γ. In other words, F is given a Γ-equivariant structure.

Conclusion (carried on the next page). This structure amounts to extending the π-action on τ to an action of the extension 𝓔 (1 → π → 𝓔 → Γ → 1, the group of pairs (γ, lift of γ to Π̃)). Grothendieck immediately notes that this gives no geometric interpretation of the 'T-structure'. He then abandons the thread and moves to section (9) on modular topoi (T_{0,ν}).
errors: No mathematical error. The statement that cocontinuous functors π-Ens → Ens are E ↦ τ ∧_π E is correct. The claimed meaning of the equivariance data (extension of the π-action on τ to the extension 𝓔) is correct up to the usual coherence conditions, which the transitivity requirement supplies. Some notation is ambiguous in the manuscript: Π (the space) versus π (its group), and τ versus τ°.

ideas.what: Rev(Π) ≃ π-Ens via E ↦ Π̃ ×_π E (coverings as π-sets via the universal cover).
ideas.modern_name: Galois correspondence / classification of coverings by the fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Poincaré, covering-space theory); Grothendieck SGA1 in the Galois-category form

ideas.what: Colimit-preserving functors π-Ens → Ens are exactly contracted products τ ∧_π (−) with a right π-set τ.
ideas.modern_name: Eilenberg–Watts-type description of cocontinuous functors on presheaf toposes (Kan extension / tensor product)
ideas.where_published: SGA 4 (Exp. IV, morphisms of toposes and points via flat/cocontinuous functors)

ideas.what: A Γ-equivariant structure on F (isomorphisms F(^γΠ') ≃ F(Π') with transitivity) is equivalent to extending the π-action on τ to an action of the extension 𝓔 of Γ by π.
ideas.modern_name: Equivariant objects / descent along BΓ; outer action ↔ group extension
ideas.where_published: Similar formalism in SGA1 Exp. VI and Giraud's Cohomologie non abélienne; not specifically on this point

deep.surprise_reason: Routine translation of an equivariance condition into an extension of group actions, inside an abandoned attempt (explicitly judged not geometrically illuminating) to encode boundary/T-structure data for outer actions. Nothing new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Top-right marginal insertion is not clearly '(π-ens : l'espace π)'. It likely refers to τ being a disjoint union of principal (homogeneous) π-sets ('l'espace principal π' or similar); uncertain.
In the vertical arrow, the struck-out label is something like 'F̃' / 'F̃₀', with E ↦ Π̃ ×_π E written below it; the arrow is marked ≀ (equivalence).
'l'indice ∘ indique qu'on a renoncé[?] les op. de π' should read roughly 'l'indice ° indique qu'on a oublié les op. de π, pour ne garder que [l'ensemble]'. The sense is forgetting the π-action.
'(qui [?] sur Rev(Π) non en fonction[?] [?] Π)' is roughly '(qui vit sur Rev(Π), i.e. en fonction des revêtements de Π)'; the gist is that F is defined on coverings of Π.
'compatible avec les foncteurs F' more plausibly reads 'compatible avec les opérations [de Γ sur Rev Π]'; the second 'F' line is likely '..., i.e. que l'on ait des isom'.
The page number written in the upper right is 13 (internal numbering); the archive page is 25.
